_why: BUILD, GROW and LAUNCH are teaching pathways. They are also three of the most ordinary verbs in English, and a games directory is full of them. The index derives the pathway facet by matching words against a record's own prose, lowercased first - which destroys the only signal separating the verb from the pathway. Nine arcade records were filed under a teaching pathway because their blurb said 'build', 'Build' or 'grow'.
_whyAClassAndNotAList: An id list fixes the nine that exist today. A class rule also catches the tenth and eleventh, which is the pair order FC nearly created when it rewrote two descriptions using the word 'grow'. The defect is the instrument, not the inputs, so the rule is scoped to the class the instrument cannot read.
_whyNotTheRealFix: The correct instrument is whole-field equality on a declared pathway field. No source record declares one, and flipping to it today would strip the facet from 558 of 717 records - a fix that breaks more than it repairs is a finding, not a fix. Deferred behind the A1 tag backfill, which now blocks two things: A2 pupil card badges AND this flip. When A1 lands, the flip's fail-closed rule is: no field, no facet - never text-guessed.
_failClosed: Consulted BEFORE the text matcher, never after. A missing, unparseable or empty record is MEASUREMENT INVALID and exits non-zero - it never falls through to the old behaviour. An exclusion record that silently vanished would restore the defect while every check stayed green.
rationale: An arcade game is not a teaching-pathway resource. Its blurb describing what a player builds or grows is prose about play, not a curriculum signal.
